_comment: Work-permit routes for skilled non-EU professionals, by country. Names and official links only. Salary thresholds change every year, so always check the official page. This is general information, not legal advice.

DE.name: EU Blue Card (Germany)
DE.notes: Recognised degree plus a job offer above the annual salary threshold (lower threshold for shortage occupations, which include IT).

DE.name: Skilled worker residence permit (§18b)
DE.notes: For qualified professionals with a recognised qualification.

NL.name: Highly Skilled Migrant (kennismigrant)
NL.notes: Employer must be a recognised sponsor with the IND. Age-dependent salary threshold.

IE.name: Critical Skills Employment Permit
IE.notes: For occupations on the Critical Skills list (many ICT roles) above the salary threshold.

IE.name: General Employment Permit
IE.notes: Usually requires a labour market needs test.

SE.name: Work permit (Sweden)
SE.notes: Job offer meeting Swedish collective-agreement terms and the minimum salary requirement.

SE.name: EU Blue Card (Sweden)
SE.notes: Higher qualifications plus a salary threshold.

DK.name: Pay Limit Scheme
DK.notes: Job offer above the annual pay limit.

DK.name: Positive List for People with a Higher Education
Fast-track scheme
DK.notes: Only via employers certified by SIRI.

FI.name: Residence permit for a specialist
FI.notes: Expert work with a higher-education degree and a salary threshold. A fast track exists.

FI.name: EU Blue Card (Finland)
FI.notes: Higher qualifications plus a salary threshold.

BE.name: Single permit, highly qualified worker
BE.notes: Rules differ by region (Brussels, Flanders, Wallonia).

BE.name: EU Blue Card (Belgium)
BE.notes: Degree plus a salary threshold set by each region.

LU.name: EU Blue Card (Luxembourg)
LU.notes: Highly qualified worker route with a salary threshold.

AT.name: Red-White-Red Card / EU Blue Card (Austria)
AT.notes: Points-based routes for very highly qualified and key workers.
